DeltaLab — Privacy policy

DeltaLab Privacy Policy

Effective date: 7 July 2026
Last updated: 30 October 2026

This policy applies to DeltaLab on the Apple App Store and on Google Play. We may update it from time to time; the "last updated" date above shows the current version.

In short

DeltaLab is a convenience client for the National Health Laboratory Service (NHLS) TrakCare lab-results portal, built for South African doctors. You sign in with your own NHLS portal credentials, and the app fetches lab results directly from the NHLS portal to your device over HTTPS.

Patient data never reaches us. No DeltaLab server receives, stores, or processes your NHLS login or any patient data. Patient results flow only between your device and NHLS — exactly as they would if you opened the NHLS portal in a web browser. We (the developer) never see them.

We collect almost nothing. There are no analytics, no tracking, no advertising, and no crash-reporting SDKs in the app. The one thing we run is a small referral service, used only if you take part in referral codes; it holds a code and an anonymous subscription ID, never anything about patients (see "Referral codes" below).

DeltaLab is free for five patients a day; an optional subscription removes that limit. The daily count is kept on your device only and is never sent to us or to anyone else.

Who we are

DeltaLab is developed by Facet Software (Pty) Ltd, a company registered in South Africa (registration number 2026/750377/07). In this policy, "we", "us" and "the developer" mean Facet Software (Pty) Ltd.

For any privacy question or request, contact: hello@facetsoftware.co.za.

What the app does

DeltaLab presents a native search-and-results interface over the NHLS TrakCare portal. When you sign in, the app authenticates to NHLS on your behalf using the credentials you entered and requests patient lab results, episodes, and PDF reports directly from NHLS. Your access, and everything you can see, is exactly what your own NHLS account already permits.

What we collect

We collect no patient data and no NHLS credentials, on any server. Almost everything the app handles stays on your device. The only personal information we hold is the referral record described under "Referral codes", and only if you use them.

The only information that ever leaves your device is:

  • Your NHLS credentials — sent only to NHLS, to log you in. They are transmitted directly to the NHLS portal over HTTPS to authenticate you. They are not sent anywhere else, and never to the developer.
  • Patient lab data — exchanged only between your device and NHLS. Requested from and returned by the NHLS portal over HTTPS. It does not pass through any developer-controlled system.
  • Subscription and update metadata — sent to Apple or Google, RevenueCat, and Expo (the third parties described below), to run the subscription and to deliver app updates. This does not include your name, email, NHLS credentials, or any patient data.
  • Referral records — sent to our referral service, only if you use referral codes. Your referral code, an anonymous subscription ID and who referred whom, as described under "Referral codes" below. No name, email, NHLS credentials or patient data.
  • Empty connectivity checks — sent to Google. While the app is open, it checks from time to time that your phone has a working internet connection (roughly once a minute, and again when a request to NHLS fails) by making an empty request to a Google connectivity-check address. That is how it can tell you "you appear to be offline" rather than wrongly blaming NHLS. The request carries no information about you or any patient.

What stays on your device

To make the app usable, some data is stored locally on your device. None of it is transmitted to the developer or to any server we control, apart from the referral key described in the last item below. All of it relies on your device's operating-system encryption.

  • NHLS credentials. Your username, password and the portal address are stored on-device only, in your device's secure storage (via expo-secure-store: the iOS Keychain on iPhone, and on Android encrypted storage protected by the Android Keystore), together with your practitioner code if you set one for the "Your results" tab. They are used solely to authenticate to NHLS and are never uploaded to us. Your login session cookie is held in memory only and is discarded when the app is terminated.
  • Recently viewed patients. When you open a patient from search results, a "Recently viewed" entry — the patient's identifying details and the results you opened — is cached on-device so you can quickly return to a recent look-up. You can switch this off in Settings → Privacy → Recently viewed.
  • Your ward-round list. Patients you star for your round are listed on-device, so the app can show you their pending tests and flag any new positive culture.
  • Linked patient records. If you link two NHLS records as the same patient on the Timeline, the app remembers that link — the identifying details shown on each linked record (name, hospital number, lab record number, sex and date of birth) — in your device's secure storage, so the timeline can merge them next time.
  • Cached results and timelines. Lab results and multi-episode timelines you have viewed may be cached on-device to speed up re-opening them.
  • PDF report cache (48 hours). Lab-report PDFs you open are cached on-device and automatically deleted after 48 hours.
  • Handover sheets. Ward-round handover PDFs you generate are saved in the app's cache so you can share them, until you clear them (see below).
  • Theme and app settings. Your display preferences and your timeline panel choices are stored locally.
  • Your free-tier daily count. So the app can tell how many patients you have opened today, it keeps a small counter in your device's secure storage: today's date, and a short scrambled code for each patient record you opened today. The code is derived from the record number using a random value created on your device; it is not the record number itself, and the counter holds no name, no hospital number and no result value. Nobody can read a list of patients out of it; someone who already knew a particular record number and had your unlocked phone could, at most, check whether that record was opened today. It is never transmitted anywhere. It only ever holds one day's worth: the first time you use the app on a new day, the previous day's entries are discarded.
  • Diagnostic records. To help us fix problems, the app keeps small technical logs on your device: lab test names it did not recognise, and — only on the developer's own internal and development builds — a record of cases where its fast first display of an episode's results disagreed with the full results that followed (which test, what kind of mismatch, when, and the lab episode number). The app you install from the App Store or Google Play never writes that second record, and has no setting that turns it on. They never contain a patient's name, hospital number, record number or any result value. They are never sent anywhere automatically. A phone that recorded the second kind under an earlier test version keeps it unread until Settings → "Clear all data & sign out", which deletes these records on every version of the app (see below).
  • Your referral key. If you use referral codes, the app keeps a random key in your device's secure storage that proves to our referral service that the code is yours. It identifies nothing about you. Our service stores only a scrambled (one-way hashed) form of it.

Because these caches contain patient information, you should protect your device with a passcode/biometrics and treat it the way you would treat any device you use to view patient records.

Deleting on-device data

You are in control of the on-device caches:

  • Recent tab → "Clear all" removes all recently viewed patients and their cached results/timelines.
  • Settings → "Clear recent views" does the same.
  • Long-press a recent entry → "Remove" deletes a single entry.
  • Settings → "Clear round list" empties your ward-round list.
  • Linked records can be removed one at a time on the patient's Timeline, or under Settings → Customisation → Panels & linked patients.
  • Settings → "Clear all data & sign out" signs you out and deletes everything above — credentials, recently viewed patients, your round list, linked records, cached results and timelines, PDFs and handover sheets, settings, diagnostic records, and your referral key and referral record — except the free-tier daily count, which is kept by design.
  • The PDF report cache clears itself automatically after 48 hours.
  • Deleting the app on iPhone removes the app's own storage, but iOS keeps Keychain items after an app is deleted. That means your saved NHLS credentials, any linked patient records, the free-tier daily count and any referral key can remain on the device after you delete DeltaLab. To remove everything the app has stored, use "Clear all data & sign out" before deleting the app; that leaves only the free-tier daily count, which contains no patient identifiers and nothing about you, and never holds more than the current day.
  • Uninstalling the app on Android removes everything it stored, including its secure storage and the free-tier daily count.
  • Android backups. Android's automatic Google backup is configured so that it never includes your NHLS credentials, linked records, the free-tier count, or any patient data or cached results; at most it copies a few non-sensitive app preferences.
  • Erasing the device removes everything, including that counter.

Third parties involved

DeltaLab relies on a small number of third parties. Each receives only what it needs for its specific function, and none of them receives patient data.

  • NHLS (National Health Laboratory Service). The source of all lab data. When you sign in, the app talks directly to the NHLS TrakCare portal using your credentials. Your use of NHLS is governed by NHLS's own terms and privacy practices and by your professional access arrangements with them.
  • Apple. DeltaLab is distributed on iPhone through the App Store. If you subscribe there, Apple processes the payment and manages the auto-renewable subscription. The developer never receives your card or payment details. Apple's handling of your data is governed by Apple's Privacy Policy.
  • Google Play. DeltaLab is distributed on Android through Google Play. If you subscribe there, Google processes the payment and manages the auto-renewable subscription. The developer never receives your card or payment details. Google's handling of your data is governed by Google's Privacy Policy.
  • RevenueCat. We use RevenueCat (the react-native-purchases SDK) to manage the subscription and verify entitlement. RevenueCat receives an anonymous app-user identifier, along with purchase/transaction history and receipt data relayed from Apple or Google. It does not receive your name, email, NHLS credentials, or any patient data. See RevenueCat's Privacy Policy.
  • Expo (EAS Update). App updates are delivered over-the-air via Expo's EAS Update service. To fetch the correct update, the app sends Expo basic device and runtime metadata (such as app version, runtime version, and platform) and a random identifier generated for this installation, which Expo uses to roll updates out gradually. It is not linked to your name, email, or NHLS account, and no patient data or credentials are involved. See Expo's Privacy Explained.
  • Cloudflare. Runs our referral service on its servers worldwide and keeps the service's records in a database in Europe, as described under "Referral codes" below, and counts visits to the DeltaLab invite page on our website, as described under "Our website". It never receives patient data or NHLS credentials. See Cloudflare's Privacy Policy.
  • Google (connectivity checks). On both iPhone and Android, as described above, the app periodically makes an empty request to a Google connectivity-check address. Google receives only what any website receives when your phone connects to it, such as your IP address — nothing about you, your NHLS account, or any patient. See Google's Privacy Policy.

The free tier and subscriptions

DeltaLab is free to use for five patients per day. The allowance resets at midnight in your device's local time; reopening a patient you have already opened that day does not count again, and patients already saved on your device stay readable once the allowance is spent. Nothing about how this is counted involves us: the count is kept on your device (see "What stays on your device" above) and is never transmitted.

An optional auto-renewable subscription removes the daily limit. It is sold and billed by Apple through your Apple ID if you use an iPhone, or by Google through your Google Play account if you use Android. Payment is handled entirely by the store; we never see your payment method. Subscription status is checked via RevenueCat as described above.

You can view, manage, or cancel your subscription at any time with the store you bought it from, or from inside DeltaLab under Settings → Manage subscription:

  • iPhone: Settings → [your name] → Subscriptions on your device, or apps.apple.com/account/subscriptions.
  • Android: Google Play Store → your profile icon → Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions, or play.google.com/store/account/subscriptions.

Cancellation and refund handling follow the store's standard terms; the developer cannot cancel a subscription on your behalf or refund an Apple subscription.

Referral codes

Taking part in referral codes and friend codes (below) is optional: you can use DeltaLab, and subscribe, without ever touching them.

They are run by a small referral service of ours, hosted by Cloudflare. The app contacts it only when you ask for your own referral code (Settings → Refer a colleague) or enter a code. Once you have a code, the app also checks your referral status when you open that card or the subscription screen. The service stores:

  • your referral code, and a scrambled (one-way hashed) form of your referral key;
  • the anonymous RevenueCat ID of each installation that uses it (the Support ID in Settings → Subscription), and whether it is Android or iPhone;
  • if you entered a colleague's code: whose code it was, and whether and when you started a free trial and made your first payment;
  • on iPhone, if you entered a colleague's code: the single-use Apple offer code we gave you to redeem with Apple;
  • if colleagues used your code: the free months you earned, and whether and when they were applied;
  • if you used a friend code (below): which code, when, and until when it gave you DeltaLab Pro;
  • when you last used it.

It never receives patient data, NHLS credentials, your name, your email or your phone number. It does not record whom you share your code with, or whether you share it at all.

Friend codes. We sometimes give friends a code for free access, named after them (for example NICK123), and a code they can pass on to people they tell about DeltaLab (for example IKNOWNICK). If you use one, the service records which code you used and when, and asks RevenueCat to give your anonymous subscription ID DeltaLab Pro for the months the code allows. Nothing is charged, and the free months end by themselves. A friend's own code is linked to the account that first uses it, and if you reinstall we can move it to your new install when you send us your new Support ID. Each person can use one of each kind of code, and a code you pass on only a limited number of times.

To check a referral and to apply a reward, the service asks RevenueCat for the subscription status of the IDs above, and asks RevenueCat to move your next payment date with Google Play or to grant your free month. On iPhone, while you subscribe through the App Store, your free month waits in the app until you claim it, and Apple then applies it at your next renewal.

Like any website, Cloudflare sees your phone's IP address when the app contacts the service. The service uses it for a few seconds at most, to limit how often codes can be tried, and never stores it. Cloudflare keeps short technical request logs, which we read only to fix faults, and deletes them automatically within a week.

Invite links. If DeltaLab is already installed, on iPhone or Android, a colleague's invite link opens the app, which reads the invite code from the link. If you install DeltaLab on Android from an invite link, Google Play tells the app which link it was installed from, and the app reads the invite code from it, once. On iPhone the App Store passes nothing on, so you type the code in yourself. Either way the app reads nothing else, shows you the code, and sends it to our service only if you choose to use it.

If a record is deleted. If you delete your referral record, a colleague who used your code keeps their own record, which then shows only that they used a code, not whose. If a colleague you referred deletes theirs, your record keeps the free month you earned and nothing that identifies them. Free months already applied stay applied. If you used a friend code, the record that it was used once stays, with nothing linking it to you, so the code's limit still holds.

Request deletion

DeltaLab has no accounts. Off your phone, the records we can delete on request are:

  • the customer record RevenueCat keeps for us under your anonymous Support ID: your subscription status and purchase history;
  • your referral record on our referral service, only if you have used referral or friend codes (see "Referral codes").

You can delete your referral record yourself, at any time, in the app: Settings → "Clear all data & sign out" deletes it from our service, along with everything else the app keeps on your phone (see "Deleting on-device data").

To have us delete these records, or if you no longer have the app or the phone, email hello@facetsoftware.co.za. Include the Support ID from Settings → Subscription (note it down before you delete the app), or tell us your referral code. We need one of them to find your records, because we hold nothing else that identifies you. Within 30 days we will delete the customer record RevenueCat keeps for us and your referral record, if you have one, and confirm by email.

Deleting these records does not cancel a subscription: cancel it with the store first (see "The free tier and subscriptions"). Apple and Google keep their own purchase records under their own policies, and Expo and Cloudflare keep the update and request data they receive under theirs (see "Data retention").

We also delete referral records automatically: see "Data retention" below.

Our website

When a colleague shares a DeltaLab referral link, it opens our invite page at facetsoftware.co.za/deltalab/invite. That page counts visits with Cloudflare Web Analytics. It sets no cookies, stores nothing on your device, and does not track you across other sites. What is counted is the page, the time, the country the visit came from, and the kind of device and browser. Like any website, Cloudflare sees your IP address when the counter loads, and uses it to work out the country. The page removes the invite code from its address before anything is counted, so a visit cannot be linked to the colleague who shared the link. The rest of our website collects nothing.

How patient data is handled, and who is responsible (POPIA)

This section matters and is written plainly.

Patient lab results are special personal information under South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act, 2013 (POPIA). In the context of DeltaLab:

  • The patient data is processed by you, the clinician, in your professional capacity, using your own NHLS access — the same access you would use in a web browser. DeltaLab is simply a different window onto the records you are already authorised to view.
  • The developer is not a processor of that patient data. We do not receive it, store it on any server, or process it on your behalf. It travels only between your device and NHLS. The on-device caches described above sit on your device, under your control.
  • You remain responsible for your own professional and POPIA obligations when viewing, storing, or otherwise handling patient information on your device — for example, keeping your device secure, only accessing records you are entitled to see, and complying with your employer's and NHLS's information-governance rules. Using DeltaLab does not change or reduce those responsibilities.

Where the app does touch your own personal information (your NHLS credentials, subscription identifiers), we aim to process it lawfully and minimally, consistent with POPIA — in practice, by keeping credentials on-device and sharing only the minimum described above with Apple or Google, RevenueCat, and Expo.

For the referral records described under "Referral codes", Facet Software (Pty) Ltd is the responsible party under POPIA. We process them because you chose to take part, and only to run the referral scheme: never for advertising, never sold, and shared only with Cloudflare and RevenueCat, who process them for us. Cloudflare keeps them in Europe, outside South Africa, under its data-processing terms with us.

Data retention

  • On-device credentials and linked patient records are retained until you remove them (Settings → "Clear all data & sign out", or for links, the controls above). On iPhone they are in the Keychain, so deleting the app alone does not remove them; on Android, uninstalling the app removes them.
  • Recently viewed patients, cached results, and timelines are retained until you clear them, or until the app evicts older entries to stay within its cache limits.
  • Your ward-round list is retained until you remove patients from it or clear it.
  • Cached PDF reports are retained for a maximum of 48 hours, then automatically deleted. Handover sheets are retained until you use "Clear all data & sign out", or until your phone's operating system clears the app's cache to free up storage.
  • Diagnostic records are capped in size, and are deleted by "Clear all data & sign out". The results-comparison record described above is kept only on the developer's own internal and development builds; the app you install never writes it, so there is nothing to retain.
  • The free-tier daily count holds only the current day's entries; they are discarded and replaced the first time you use the app on a new day. If you stop using the app entirely, the last day's entries stay in secure storage until you next open it or erase the device. On iPhone it survives app deletion (see above); on Android, uninstalling removes it.
  • Your referral key, if you use referral codes, is retained in secure storage until you use "Clear all data & sign out". Like the free-tier count, on iPhone it survives app deletion; on Android, uninstalling removes it.
  • The developer retains none of the above, because none of it is transmitted to us.
  • Referral records on our service are deleted automatically 24 months after the last activity involving them: the last time your app checked your referral status, or a colleague's use of your code, trial, payment or reward. You can delete them sooner (see "Request deletion"). The service also keeps the ID and time of each subscription event RevenueCat sends it, so that it never counts one twice, for 90 days. Apple offer codes are deleted 30 days after Apple's own expiry date for them; one you were given stops being linked to you as soon as your referral record is deleted.
  • Apple or Google, RevenueCat, Expo and Cloudflare retain the subscription, update and request data they receive according to their own retention policies (linked above).

Your rights

The only personal information we hold on a server is your referral record, and only if you use referral codes. You can see what matters in it (your code and the free months you have earned) in the app, delete it there, or ask us for a copy of it or to delete it, along with the customer record RevenueCat keeps for us (see "Request deletion"). Everything else stays on your device, and you can delete it yourself using the controls above.

For the personal information held by third parties:

  • Patient records: direct requests to NHLS, the data custodian.
  • Subscription/payment data: exercise your rights through Apple or Google, and RevenueCat.
  • Update metadata: exercise your rights through Expo.

Under POPIA you have rights to access and correct your personal information, to object to processing in certain circumstances, and to lodge a complaint with the Information Regulator of South Africa (inforeg@justice.gov.za). If you have any question about how DeltaLab handles data, email us first at hello@facetsoftware.co.za and we will help point you to the right place.

Security

  • NHLS credentials and linked patient records are stored in the operating system's protected credential storage: the iOS Keychain on iPhone, and storage encrypted with the Android Keystore on Android.
  • Other on-device caches rely on your phone's built-in device encryption (iOS or Android); protect your device with a passcode and biometrics.
  • All communication with NHLS, and with the third-party services above, is over HTTPS.
  • The session cookie is kept in memory only and discarded when the app terminates.
  • Our referral service stores your referral key only in hashed form, so its records alone cannot be used to act as you.

No method of storage or transmission is perfectly secure, but we have designed the app so that the developer never becomes a holder of your sensitive data — your NHLS login or any patient data — in the first place.

Children

DeltaLab is a professional tool for healthcare practitioners. It is not directed at children and is not intended for use by anyone under 18. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. (Note that a clinician may legitimately view the lab records of paediatric patients through their NHLS access — that data is handled as described in the POPIA section above and never reaches the developer.)

Changes to this policy

We may update this policy as the app evolves. When we do, we will change the "last updated" date at the top, and — for material changes — mention it in the app's release notes. Continued use after an update means you accept the revised policy.
